(Search snippet content — outlets' own reporting language, cross-referenced across
five approved sources.)

- On 15 July 2026 President Zelensky announced the dismissal of defence minister
  Mykhailo Fedorov as part of a wider cabinet reshuffle. Fedorov pushed battlefield
  innovation through the use of drones and was an architect of Ukraine's drone
  programme.
- Large protests erupted in several Ukrainian cities on Thursday. More than a thousand
  people rallied in Kyiv's central square, waving Ukrainian and EU flags and chanting
  "shame" and "bring Fedorov back".
- Pavlo Yelizarov, a deputy commander of Ukraine's air force, announced on Facebook he
  was stepping down in response to the dismissal.
- Two of Fedorov's advisers resigned in protest.
- The Verkhovna Rada is reported to be reluctant to vote in a new defence minister.
- Volodymyr Fesenko, head of the Kyiv-based Penta think tank, said the rallies,
  protest resignations and parliamentary reluctance prove Zelensky faces "a stalemate
  situation".
- At a press conference in Kyiv with Keir Starmer, Zelensky acknowledged tension
  between commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrsky and Fedorov, saying they could not work
  together unless he acted as mediator.
